results.claim: The arbitrary-sharing-number no-teleport problem belongs to NP.
results.proof_sketch: Let L be the total number of feature occurrences. Every no-teleport transition goes between distinct tiles having a live common feature and deletes at least one occurrence at each endpoint, hence at least two occurrences. A play therefore has at most floor(L/2) transitions, so its tile sequence is a polynomial-length certificate. A verifier stores which occurrences remain live; for each consecutive pair it checks distinctness and a nonempty live-feature intersection, deletes every feature live at both endpoints, and finally checks that no occurrence remains. This is polynomial time. Also, no unordered tile pair can recur: its first traversal deletes every feature then live at both endpoints, and deleted occurrences never return.

results.claim: There is an exact characterization by perfect matchings plus an ordered Euler trail with precedence constraints.
results.proof_sketch: For each feature f with support S_f, choose a perfect matching M_f and let H be the simple union of these matchings. Write m_f(v) for v's matching edge. The required condition is an Euler-trail ordering tau of H such that whenever e=uv is not in M_f but u,v are in S_f, either tau(m_f(u))<tau(e) or tau(m_f(v))<tau(e). Necessity follows from any solution: the moves that delete f pair S_f, every move deletes some feature and hence belongs to H, repeated unordered pairs are impossible, and a nonmatching f-edge can occur only after f has been deleted at an endpoint. For sufficiency, suppose the earliest matching incidence m_f(u)=uv that fails finds f already deleted at u by an earlier edge uw. That earlier edge is nonmatching for f. Since uv occurs later, its precedence disjunction forces m_f(w) before uw. By earliest choice, m_f(w) successfully deleted f at w, so uw could not have deleted f at u—a contradiction. Thus every matching edge deletes its intended occurrences. Every H-edge belongs to some matching, so every transition is legal, and all occurrences are deleted.

results.claim: If every occurring feature appears on exactly two tiles, no-teleport solvability is decidable in linear time even with unbounded sharing number.
results.proof_sketch: For a feature supported on exactly {u,v}, only transition uv can delete it, and both occurrences remain live until that transition. Form a simple graph K by placing edge uv whenever at least one feature has those endpoints; parallel features are collapsed. A solution must traverse every edge of K, and every legal transition is such an edge. Conversely, an Euler trail of K deletes all parallel features when their edge is traversed. Thus the instance is solvable exactly when the edge-bearing vertices of K are connected and K has zero or two odd-degree vertices; a featureless instance is trivially solved. Under the standard array-indexed word-RAM occurrence representation, endpoint pairs can be obtained by scanning occurrences, nonempty tile identifiers compressed, the integer pairs radix-sorted and deduplicated, and connectivity and parity tested, all in O(L) time. Arbitrarily many features may share one endpoint pair.

results.claim: The obvious static relaxation—choosing feature-perfect-matchings whose simple union is Eulerian—is not sufficient.
results.proof_sketch: Take supports {0,1}, {0,2}, {1,2}, {0,1,2,3}, and {0,1,2,4}. The first three force the core triangle. Tiles 3 and 4 each have only their respective four-support feature, so each has exactly one incident move and they must be the trail endpoints. Their attachment edges join core vertices i and j. If i differs from j, the move graph has four odd vertices; hence i=j. Starting at 3, the trail must use 3i, traverse the triangle as a circuit based at i, and finish with i4. The first triangle edge from i deletes at i the feature supported on {0,1,2,4}, so i4 is not legal. Reversing the trail yields the symmetric contradiction. Nevertheless, matchings 03+12 and 04+12 for the four-support features, together with forced matchings 01, 02, and 12, have simple union {01,02,12,03,04}, which is connected with exactly odd vertices 3 and 4. Thus an Eulerian static union alone is insufficient.

results.claim: An exact state-space algorithm runs in O(n^2 L·2^L) time and O(n·2^L) space.
results.proof_sketch: Use states (v,M), where v is the current tile and M is the L-bit live-occurrence mask. For each of the at most n-1 possible next tiles, scan the incidence representation to find every feature live at both endpoints. If none exists, the transition is forbidden; otherwise clear both endpoint occurrences of every such feature and recurse. Every transition strictly decreases the number of live occurrences, so the recurrence is acyclic and memoized reachability is exact. There are at most n·2^L states, with O(nL) work per state, and all initial tiles can share one table. A directly indexed memo table uses O(n·2^L) space.

final_writeup:
Let S_f denote the tiles containing feature f. The principal progress is an exact separation of the static and temporal parts of the problem. Any solution induces a perfect matching M_f on every S_f. The simple union H of those matchings is precisely the edge set traversed by the solution, so it has an Euler trail.

Eulerianity of H is not sufficient. Its trail order must satisfy a precedence condition: whenever an H-edge joins two f-tiles not matched to each other, at least one endpoint's f-matching edge must have occurred earlier. Conversely, this condition is sufficient. An earliest failed matching edge would imply that an earlier nonmatching edge deleted one endpoint; precedence then places the other endpoint's successful matching edge still earlier, contradicting the claim that the nonmatching edge performed that deletion. This proves the ordered-matching characterization.

The five-tile construction shows that the temporal condition cannot be discarded even when the selected matching union is connected with exactly two odd vertices. In a different direction, when every feature has frequency two, every matching is forced and there are no nonmatching edges within a feature support. The problem then reduces to the ordinary Euler-trail criterion after parallel endpoint pairs are collapsed, despite the sharing number being unbounded.

The general problem is also in NP and admits an exact O(n^2 L·2^L)-time state-space algorithm. These results preserve substantial partial progress, but they do not supply either a polynomial-time algorithm or a hardness result for arbitrary sharing number. The target's complete complexity classification therefore remains unresolved, and claimed_resolution remains PARTIAL.
